subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & SLA language for Acme deployment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-08T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Performance follow-up & next steps (latency/throughput targets)

Thanks for taking the time today, Jordan — great discussion on your production goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Objective: Support Acme's customer chat and product search features with predictable sub-100ms UX for streaming responses and bulk reranking for search.
- Targets you mentioned on the call: P95 latency <= 120ms, P99 latency <= 300ms for short chat requests (<= 256 tokens); sustained throughput target ~250 requests/sec with bursts up to 600r/s during peak events; concurrent sessions ~400.
- Streaming: you need token-level streaming with first-byte latency < 50ms and steady token throughput for responses that stream (e.g., chat replies).
- Measurement: suggested measurement window is 30-day rolling with daily aggregates and monthly reporting.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short SLO proposal (acme-slo-proposal.pdf) and a draft SLA (redwood-sla-draft.docx) that maps the SLOs to remedies.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm the finalized numeric targets above (P95/P99/throughput/concurrency/streaming).
2) Share a small representative test workload (JSON or k6 script) so we can run a pre-engagement perf pass.
3) Agree on measurement definition: TTL, error definition, exclusions (maintenance/force majeure), and reporting cadence.
4) Procurement: review the SLA draft; I'll loop Connor for contract redlines.

If that sounds right I'll run the perf pass with Rishi and share the test results and an updated SLA with explicit measurement language.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance follow-up & next steps (latency/throughput targets)

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A couple clarifying Qs before procurement starts reviewing the SLA: 

1) When you say P95 <= 120ms, is that measured end-to-end from our API to first token, or only server-side generation time? We need to understand what to instrument.
2) For streaming first-byte latency <50ms — is that a 95th percentile across tokens, or first-token latency only?
3) Regarding exclusions: we have planned maintenance windows (weekly patching) and occasional CDN issues. Would those be excluded from SLA calculations?

Also, can you confirm the reporting cadence and what evidence you will provide (raw logs, dashboard snapshots, or both)? Procurement is sensitive to remedies — are credits the only remedy, or do you offer step-in support / escalation SLAs for critical incidents?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that's easier.

—Jordan
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance follow-up & next steps (latency/throughput targets)

Great questions — answers below and I've highlighted the bits we typically put into the SLA language so procurement has clear text to review.

1) Measurement: Latency definitions in the draft SLA are server-side e2e between when Redwood receives the HTTP request and when the first token is emitted to the client. For clarity, we define "Request Received" as the time the request hits Redwood's front-door ingress and "First Token Emitted" as when the first response byte is available on the TCP stream to your agent. If you prefer measuring from your client-side instrumentation, we can add a joint measurement appendix.

2) Streaming latency: The SLO for streaming first-byte latency is P95 of first-token latency across requests. We also include a rolling P50 median for developer visibility. We do not measure per-token latency (that's typically noisy) but we can include an optional per-token tail if you need it for debugging.

3) Exclusions: Standard exclusions in the draft SLA are: scheduled maintenance windows (we propose a weekly 60-min maintenance window), customer-induced outages (e.g., abusive traffic, misconfiguration), and force majeure. CDN issues upstream will be evaluated case-by-case; if the outage is in our network path we exclude it only if it's caused by a third-party CDN provider and you've confirmed no Redwood-run path substitution was possible.

Reporting/ evidence: Our standard is weekly automated reports + monthly executive summary. Evidence bundle includes daily CSV latency histograms, raw request/response sample logs for incidents (redacted per privacy policy), and a link to the per-route dashboard in Redwood Console. We can instrument a signed data export to your S3 if required.

Remedies: For commercial customers we typically offer service credits tied to monthly availability and SLO breaches (e.g., 5% credit for a single monthly breach, scaling with severity). For enterprise contracts we can negotiate additional operational remedies — guaranteed TTR for Sev1 incidents, assigned account reliability engineer, and accelerated escalation paths. We can outline those as options.

I'll attach a small edit to the SLA doc with explicit measurement language (redwood-sla-draft.docx).

Would you like to schedule a 30-min call with Rishi and Connor to walk procurement through the draft? Connor will handle redlines and I'll have Rishi outline the perf test plan.

Thanks,
Marissa
---
Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.docx (updated)
From: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance follow-up & next steps (latency/throughput targets)

Hi Marissa — procurement here. A few requests from legal/finance after a quick review of the SLA draft: 

- Remedies: credits-only approach is OK but we need clearer caps and a 12-month lookback on repeated breaches. Is there a maximum aggregate credit cap? Please include explicit calculation examples.
- Reporting cadence: weekly CSVs are fine; we need monthly certified reports signed by an authorized Redwood rep for audit purposes.
- Measurement window: suggest a 90-day rolling window for P99 calculations to avoid volatility from short-term bursts. Would Redwood accept 90-day for P99 but keep 30-day for P95?
- Exclusions: we need the ability to dispute exclusions with a 10-business-day review period and an arbitration clause for unresolved disputes.

Also — for our procurement process, we need a simple statement of what logs/PII will be shared in the evidence bundle and confirmation that any exported logs will be hosted in the us-west-2 region (data residency).

Can you update the draft and send back for final review this week?

Thanks,
Acme Procurement
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance follow-up & next steps (latency/throughput targets)

Appreciate the clear list — we can accommodate all of these items. Quick responses inline and next steps: 

- Remedies & caps: We'll add explicit credit calculation examples and an aggregate cap (suggested 15% of monthly invoice) — happy to discuss if your finance team wants a different ceiling.
- Certified monthly reports: we can provide a signed monthly SLA report (PDF) from Redwood's compliance team.

- Measurement window: acceptable to set P99 on a 90-day rolling window and P95 on 30-day rolling. I'll reflect that in the draft.

- Dispute process: we'll add a 10-business-day dispute review clause and an arbitration fallback as you requested.

- Data residency / logs: evidence exports can be hosted in us-west-2. Logs will be redacted to remove customer PII per our data handling policy. We'll include a short appendix that enumerates fields shared in the evidence bundle.

Next steps: Connor will send the updated redline of the SLA by EOD tomorrow. Rishi and I will schedule the perf run once you confirm the test workload (Jordan). I've cc'd Connor & Rishi to coordinate redlines and perf timeline.

If procurement is happy with the proposed credit cap and certified monthly reports, we can aim to finalize the SLA and move to contract signature next week.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
